newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crude differentials firm on closed arbitrage.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crude differentials firm on closed arbitrage.

text.p: U.S. crude grade differentials gained strength Wednesday on the continuing lack of arbitrage opportunities for foreign crudes, traders said.
Outright crude drifted lower on extended bouts of profit-taking, depressing the cash markets as well.
"Looking at the December WTI to Brent, you see the foreign crudes getting more expensive, driving up the domestics," said a crude broker.
The Dec WTI/Brent spread was hovering around 65 cts.
November West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was more than 60 cts lower at $24.75-85, and the Nov/Dec WTI spread at 36 cts.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James traded at 58 cts over WTI/Cushing, 4-6 cts higher than deals seen Tuesday.
Midland/WTI was hovering between 4-6 cts over the WTI, around the same levels seen yesterday, with little fresh direction noticed.
Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire was steady at 45 cts over WTI. November Postings Plus was heard traded at #2.12, slightly higher than Tuesday, but again with only thin volume.
Sour grades were well-positioned at current ranges, talked at $1.40-$1.36 under the marker, and Eugene Island at minus $1.15-$1.05 to the WTI/Cushing.
